extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, employers, employees, patent attorneys and IP practitioners in Turkey
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules, substantive standards and rights allocation under Turkish patent law covering duration/fees, amendments, publication, ownership disputes, employee inventions, transformations between patent and utility model, withdrawals, registration, continuation/restoration and related timelines and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of decisions on the Bulletin
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of nullity, final decisions following objections, and decisions confirming transformation or withdrawal shall be published on the Bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever the Board or Office issues a decision (nullity, continuation with amended version, confirmation of transformation, withdrawal publication, re-recognition, registration of legal proceedings), that decision is to be published on the Office Bulletin as specified in the Articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to object to Office decisions (time limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent applicant, the patentee or related third parties shall object to the decisions of the Office within two months as of the date of the notification of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections under this article are evaluated by the Board. This two-month deadline applies without prejudice to Article 99 provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting with the application date, the time period of the patent protection is twenty years; the time period of the protection of the utility model is ten years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These time periods shall not be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual fees schedule and due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual fees for protecting a patent application or patent are paid starting at the end of the second year and then annually; the due date is the month and day corresponding to the application date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are paid during the patent protection period from the application date; Office regulations determine detailed procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late payment window with surcharge
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual fees can be paid together with surcharges within six months following the due date if not paid on time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a six-month grace period for late payment subject to surcharge; further default consequences described separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of non-payment and re-validation
rubrics_metrics.description: If annual fees are not paid within the allowed time, the patent right shall expire as of the due date; the Office will notify expiration and publish it; payment of the compensatory fee within two months of notification re-validates the patent as of the payment date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office must make the expiration notification at latest until the end of one year from the original due date. Re-validation does not affect third parties' acquired rights; extent of such rights is determined by court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party analysis of unpublished applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Not yet published patent applications cannot be analysed by third parties without written permission of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: third parties who can prove that the patentee intends to use the rights provided by the application against them may analyse the unpublished application without permission. Also, where divided or successor applications are published certain prior applications may be analysed before publication. Detailed procedures are set by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and corrections to applications/patents (scope limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent application may be amended by the applicant provided amendments do not exceed the extent of the first version during Office processing; a patentee may change the patent if an objection is pending provided changes do not exceed the extent of protection granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spelling mistakes and obvious factual mistakes in patent documents shall be corrected upon request. Detailed procedures and limits determined by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation between patent and utility model (requests and timelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent applicant may request transformation of a pending patent application into a utility model application; a utility model applicant may request transformation into a patent application within three months following notification of the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such a demand is made the Office requests required documents within one month and a search fee. Failure to fulfill conditions within time means transformation request is considered not made. Same priority right carries over; retransformation requests are not admitted. Decisions are published on the Bulletin; further procedure by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of patent application (timing and effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application may be withdrawn by the applicant any time before declaration of patent grant; withdrawal of a published application shall be published and is irrevocable after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application cannot be withdrawn without consent of third parties who have rights from the application and are listed in the registry. After withdrawal, new applications may be filed in some contexts but if a published application is withdrawn, reapplication for same subject is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and effect against bona fide third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent application and patent shall be registered in a public registry; rights provided by an application or patent take effect against bona fide third persons as of the date of registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified copies provided on payment of fee; registration/publication/grant rules determined by regulation. Rights cannot be asserted against bona fide third parties unless registered in due form. Parties asserting rights must inform the patent/application number in dealings and in product labeling/advertising the number must be specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of processes (request after missing a time limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who fails to comply with a procedural time period can request continuation of the processes (with a paid fee) within two months of notification of the outcome of noncompliance; if approved, legal consequences of noncompliance are treated as not having occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request filed within two months of notification; failure to timely request leads to denial. Specific exceptions and further rules determined in other Articles/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-recognition (restoration) of rights following loss due to time noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If noncompliance with a time period caused denial, withdrawal, nullification, or loss of rights, re-recognition can be requested with fee within two months from elimination of the cause, provided the missed time period is not exceeded by more than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved, legal consequences are considered not occurred; the decision and re-recognition will be published on Bulletin. During lapse until publication, bona fide third parties who used or took firm actions may continue to use free of charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on continuation/re-recognition requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation of processes cannot be requested for restoration fee time (Article 101(4)), the time period in Article 93(1), and time periods determined by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain statutory time limits are excluded from continuation/re-recognition remedies; detailed scope set by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect processes — cancellation and restart
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for nullity grounds specified elsewhere, if an incorrect continuation of proceedings is detected (by objection or ex officio), the incorrect transaction and subsequent transactions shall be cancelled and the process restarted from the phase at which the mistake was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures procedural integrity where mistakes occurred in processing applications or certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent ownership default rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claim right belongs to the inventor or their successor; if invention made jointly it belongs to all unless otherwise decided; if same invention made independently by more than one person, right belongs to the earlier application provided it is published; the first applicant is presumed owner until proven otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are presumptions and default ownership rules; disputes handled by court actions as described in subsequent Articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office stance and procedure for ownership disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall not suggest that patent claim right does not belong to the applicant; any party alleging true ownership must bring an action and report it to the Office; the court may suspend patent granting until finalization of the legal proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If court decides the plaintiff is the true owner, remedies follow (demand Office consider and perform the application as theirs, make new application with priority, or demand denial). Time-limited actions and effects specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and deadlines for successful ownership claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: If decision finalizes in plaintiff’s favour, within three months the plaintiff can (a) demand the Office consider and perform the patent application as theirs; (b) make a new application for the same invention benefiting from priority; (c) demand denial of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If plaintiff does not act within three months, the subject application is considered withdrawn. These rules also apply to divided applications; partial joint ownership claims are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent disseizor claims and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A person claiming to be the true owner (patent disseizor) may demand the court to grant the patent to themselves; claims (and partial claims) can be performed within two years from publication of patent grant, or if malicious intent, until the end of patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings and final decisions are registered and published on the Bulletin and generate effect against bona fide third parties as of registry date. Changes of ownership may terminate third-party licenses; transitional non-monopolized licenses may be ordered by court on equitable terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for third-party licensees when ownership changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon change of patent ownership under these rules, third parties’ license rights regarding the patent and other recognized rights expire with registry of the change; prior bona fide users may be entitled to a non-monopolized license from the true patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribed time periods to claim such rights differ: two months for individuals already known as true patentee on the registry and four months for the patent receiver, counting from Office notification of registration. Terms issued should be reasonable and may be modeled on compulsory license provisions; malicious actors are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership/indivisibility of patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent application or patent belongs to more than one individual, partnership rights follow agreement between parties or, absent agreement, joint ownership law; every right holder can independently perform certain acts (use share, use invention after announcing, take protective measures, bring legal proceedings but must notify co-owners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consensus of right holders required to issue licenses to third parties; if consensus impossible, court may grant authority to one or a few right holders on equitable basis. A patent application or patent cannot be divided to transfer or generate rights despite multiple owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: in-service (employee) vs independent invention
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention made in the course of duties in a facility or public agency or substantially based on experience and work in such an entity is an in-service invention; other inventions are independent inventions. Students/interns working unpaid with no time limitation are treated under employee provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules apply to state institution workers and research infrastructures under other laws; minimum payments and caps for state worker inventions specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify employer of in-service invention (content & timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Workers who make an in-service invention must report it in writing without delay, explaining the technical problem, the solution, how they made it, providing pictures if helpful, and detailing experiences/other workers’ contributions and instructions received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer must acknowledge date of receipt in writing without delay and inform worker within two months which aspects require reorganization of the report. Employer must help the worker to make proper notification. Worker must keep the in-service invention confidential unless it acquires independent invention qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer's claim to rights on in-service inventions (timing & effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer may demand full or partial rights on the in-service invention and must notify this demand in writing within four months of receiving the worker’s notification; failure to notify or a notification not demanding rights means invention acquires independent status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If employer claims full rights, all rights transfer to employer upon notification. If partial rights claimed, invention remains independent but employer may use the invention per partial rights; worker may offer employer to undertake full rights or renounce partial rights and if employer fails to respond within two months partial rights expire. Commitments made by worker before employer claims are invalid to the extent they violate employer’s rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration and factors for calculating worker's rate
rubrics_metrics.description: If employer claims full rights the worker can demand a reasonable amount; if employer claims partial rights and uses the invention, the worker can demand payment. In calculating the rate, consider the economic evaluability of the invention, the worker’s job in the business, and the business’s contribution to the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer cannot avoid payment by alleging invention not worth protection unless a court confirms nonpatentability. Method of payment should follow agreement between parties; rate tariff and arbitration procedures for disputes are determined by regulation. Payments and methods are separately determined for multiple workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer obligation to apply for patent when claiming full rights and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If employer claims full rights they are obliged to file the first patent application to the Office, unless filing is avoided for business interests; exceptions where obligation vanishes include (a) invention becoming independent, (b) worker consents not to file, (c) protecting company secrets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worker may personally apply if invention becomes independent. If the employer does not file within the time period determined by the worker, the invention acquires independent status. Employer may file applications abroad and reserve non-monopolized rights for a fee; employer must facilitate worker obtaining patents in countries where employer does not wish to obtain patent, timely to preserve priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory fairness of employer–worker agreements on inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer regulations and agreements contrary to the statutory provisions on workers’ inventions are not allowed; contract authorization regarding workers’ inventions begins after patent application for in-service inventions and after notification for independent inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements and determined rates that are not considerably equitable are invalid even if not contrary to mandatory statutory facts. Objections to inequitable agreements/rates can be made in writing at latest six months after the end of the employment contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' procedural obligations regarding worker inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Worker must provide necessary information and assistance to obtain a patent; employer must provide worker with copies of applications and supplemental documents, and inform progress upon request. Before paying the worker’s rate, employer must notify worker if renouncing the patent application or rights; upon worker’s request employer must transfer rights/documents at worker’s cost; if worker fails to respond to employer notification within three months the employer can renounce the application and rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer may reserve a non-monopolized right for a decent fee when renouncing. Rights and obligations from worker invention persist after expiration of work contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent invention notification and employer objection window
rubrics_metrics.description: If a worker makes an independent invention while employed, the worker must notify the employer without delay providing information sufficient to determine whether invention is truly independent; employer may object in writing within three months of the notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worker is not obliged to notify if it is clear the independent invention is outside the employer’s field of activity.
